tools.name: decode_plate
tools.description:
When a UK plate of this format could have been issued, from the plate alone (format, age identifier, and the
    window as first and last month). Offline: it does not look the car up; use free_check for that. No account needed.

tools.name: free_check
tools.description:
The site's free check: identity, tax and MOT status, latest MOT test, its defects and recorded mileage,
    the existing since-previous-test summary and mileage-unverified flag. Includes presentation, up to three
    questions from these free facts, a verdict image, locked teasers and a report link.

tools.name: resolve_vehicle
tools.description:
Resolve a typed plate, car photo data URL or supported advert URL to a plate only. No account or spend.
    If uncertain, ask the user to confirm; if unavailable, ask for the typed plate. Then use free_check.

tools.name: compare_vehicles
tools.description:
Compare the site's free projections for exactly two plates: identity, status and latest MOT test.
    Duplicate plates use one lookup. Includes questions from free facts, comparison image and report links.
    No prediction-based ranking; next-MOT estimates and likely repairs stay in the detailed re

tools.name: sample_report
tools.description:
The detailed report and viewing advice for one public sample car (CX52HHM, a 2002 Land Rover Defender), to show
    what a detailed report contains. Use when the user asks what RegTail's detailed report looks like. No account needed.
    It is always the same sample car, never the user's car.

tools.name: full_report
tools.description:
The detailed report of a car the user has unlocked on their RegTail account: verdict and top risks, every MOT test
    with defects and advisories, mileage analysis, recurring advisories, other sections,
    the viewing checklist, what was not checked, and guidance for explaining it. Use to discuss

tools.name: unlock_report
tools.description:
Spends one of the user's RegTail credits to unlock the detailed report for this plate for 30 days, then returns
    the detailed report (as full_report does). Ask the user first, every time, and call this only after they agree; never
    unlock on your own initiative or to answer a general question.

tools.name: viewing_advice
tools.description:
Advice for viewing an unlocked car in person: a summary, priorities to check (each with why and the report
    records behind it) and known weak spots of the model. Needs the user's RegTail account linked and the plate
    unlocked; never spends.

tools.name: credits_balance
tools.description:
How many credits the user's RegTail account holds, and pricing_url, a page explaining how credits work. Needs
    the user's RegTail account linked.

tools.name: my_reports
tools.description:
The cars the user has unlocked (with when each unlock ends) and their recent checks, so a conversation can pick
    up a car checked earlier. Needs the user's RegTail account linked.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "sample_report" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "full_report" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: The detailed report of a car the user has unlocked on their RegTail account: verdict and top risks, every MOT test with defects and advisories, mileage analysis…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
